title: Microsoft Copilot Dashboard: export day-level Copilot metrics
summary: The briefing's export behaviour, default, licensing prerequisites and rollout targets are supported by Microsoft sources. Minor corrections would make the policy paths self-contained and align the governance checklist with the controls table.

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified at 2026-09-08T22:57:21.
The roadmap describes exporting fresher row-level Copilot metrics from the Copilot Dashboard for reporting and deeper analysis at day level.
claims.quote: This feature enables users to export fresher row-level Copilot metrics from the Copilot Dashboard for reporting and deeper analysis at day level.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; controls[0].governs
claims.claim: The day-level export is added alongside an existing user-week export.
claims.quote: In addition to the existing user-week export (see MC1173208), dashboard users with company-level access will be able to export a subset of de-identified Copilot usage metrics aggregated by user and day.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The new export provides row-level Copilot usage metrics aggregated by user and day.
claims.quote: A new export option will allow eligible users to download de-identified, row-level Copilot usage metrics aggregated by user and day, covering the most recent 28 days.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Each day-level export contains 28 days of aggregated metrics.
claims.quote: Each day-level export contains 28 days of aggregated metrics with removed identifiers.

claims.where: What's changing; summary; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Personal identifiers are replaced with anonymised IDs unless the administrator has enabled identifiable export for the user.
claims.quote: Personal identifiers are removed and replaced with anonymized IDs, unless your administrator has enabled identifiable export for you. If your administrator has enabled identifiable export, the export also includes identifiable fields.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Users select Export data in the Copilot Dashboard and then Export by day to download the day-level file.
claims.quote: Eligible tenants and users can export directly from the Copilot Dashboard by selecting Export data. ... Select Export by week, to download the last six months of data; or select Export by day, to download the last 28 days of data.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Autonomy & actions

claims.claim: The export policy path is Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > Access setting, with the app and feature choices supplied in the row note.
claims.quote: Select the Settings tab and select Manage feature access. ... Select Create a policy. ... Name the policy and select the app and feature for which you'd like to set the policy. ... Select the Access setting option
claims.fix: Make the path self-contained by including the target app and feature already given in the note: 'Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > Viva Insights > Copilot Metrics Export > Access setting'. The printed steps are in the documented order; the note currently supplies the omitted target selection.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId <FeatureId from Get-VivaModuleFeature> -Name <policy name> -IsFeatureEnabled $false -Everyone creates a tenant-wide disabling policy for the selected feature.
claims.quote: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId Reflection -Name DisableFeatureForAll -IsFeatureEnabled $false -Everyone ... This example adds a policy for the Reflection feature in Viva Insights. The policy disables the feature for all users in the organization.

claims.claim: Feature access policies can target the tenant, groups or users for this feature.
claims.quote: Features support org-wide and user/group policies, unless otherwise noted in an app's feature documentation.

claims.claim: The web-app policy path is Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > Access setting, with the web-app target supplied in the note.
claims.quote: Select the Settings tab and select Manage feature access. ... Select Create a policy. ... Name the policy and select the app and feature for which you'd like to set the policy. ... Select the Access setting option
claims.fix: Make the path self-contained by including the target app and feature already given in the note: 'Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > Viva Insights > Viva Insights web app > Access setting'. The printed steps are in the documented order; the note currently supplies the omitted target selection.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId "Viva Insights web app" -Name DisableFeatureForAll -IsFeatureEnabled $false -Everyone creates a tenant-wide disabling policy for the web app.
claims.quote:
Example: Turn off the Viva Insights web app for all users in your tenant ... ModuleId : VivaInsights
FeatureId : Viva Insights web app
Name : DisableFeatureForAll
IsFeatureEnabled : false
Everyone
